title: Fluid Mechanics: Numerical Practice Set 1 (Moderate to Hard)
instructions: All 40 questions are numerical, of moderate to hard level. Keep rough paper ready.
Take g = 9.81 m/s² and the density of water as 1000 kg/m³ unless the question says otherwise.

questions.question: A flat plate of area 0.5 m² is pulled at 1.5 m/s over a fixed plate, separated from it by a 2 mm film of oil of viscosity 0.8 Pa·s. Assuming a linear velocity profile, the force needed is:
An oil has a dynamic viscosity of 0.045 Pa·s and a specific gravity of 0.9. Its kinematic viscosity is:
questions.explanation: ν = μ / ρ = 0.045 / 900 = 5 × 10⁻⁵ m²/s. Since 1 stoke = 10⁻⁴ m²/s, ν = 0.5 stokes.

questions.question: A clean glass tube of 2 mm diameter is dipped vertically in water. The surface tension is 0.0735 N/m and the contact angle is zero. Taking the unit weight of water as 9810 N/m³, the capillary rise is approximately:
The surface tension of water in contact with air is 0.072 N/m. The pressure inside a water droplet of 1 mm diameter, in excess of the outside pressure, is:
questions.explanation: For a droplet, Δp = 4σ / d = 4 × 0.072 / 0.001 = 288 Pa.

questions.question: When the pressure on a liquid is increased by 10 MPa, its volume decreases by 0.5%. Its bulk modulus of elasticity is:

A U-tube mercury manometer is connected to a pipe carrying water. The mercury surface in the limb joined to the pipe is 0.1 m below the pipe centre, and the mercury in the open limb stands 0.2 m higher. Taking the specific gravity of mercury as 13.6 and γ_w = 9.81 kN/m³, the gauge pressure in the pipe is approximately:
questions.explanation: Equating pressures at the lower mercury surface: p + 9.81 × 0.1 = 13.6 × 9.81 × 0.2. So p = 9.81 × (2.72 − 0.1) ≈ 25.70 kPa.

questions.question: A vertical rectangular gate is 2 m wide and 3 m deep, with its top edge at the water surface. Taking γ_w = 9.81 kN/m³, the total hydrostatic force on the gate is:
A vertical rectangular gate is 2 m wide and 3 m deep, with its top edge 1 m below the water surface. The depth of the centre of pressure below the water surface is:
A circular plate of 2 m diameter is immersed vertically in water with its centre 3 m below the surface. Taking γ_w = 9.81 kN/m³, the total hydrostatic force on one face is approximately:
A pressure of 200 kPa is to be expressed as a head of oil of specific gravity 0.8. Taking γ_w = 9.81 kN/m³, the head is approximately:
A wooden block of specific gravity 0.6 measures 1 m × 1 m in plan and is 0.5 m high. It floats in water with its 1 m × 1 m face horizontal. The depth of immersion is:
questions.explanation: Weight = weight of water displaced, so depth of immersion = S × height = 0.6 × 0.5 = 0.30 m.

questions.question: A rectangular pontoon is 10 m long and 6 m wide and floats in water at a draft of 1.5 m. Its centre of gravity is 2.2 m above the base. The metacentric height is:
questions.explanation: BM = I / V = (10 × 6³ / 12) / (10 × 6 × 1.5) = 180 / 90 = 2.0 m. The centre of buoyancy is 0.75 m above the base. GM = 0.75 + 2.0 − 2.2 = 0.55 m.

questions.question: A solid body weighs 500 N in air and 300 N when fully immersed in water. Its specific gravity is:
questions.explanation: Loss of weight = weight of water displaced = 200 N. Specific gravity = 500 / 200 = 2.5.

questions.question: A 300 mm diameter pipe carrying water at 2 m/s divides into a 200 mm pipe and a 150 mm pipe. The velocity in the 200 mm pipe is 1.5 m/s. The velocity in the 150 mm pipe is approximately:
questions.explanation: By continuity, d₁²V₁ = d₂²V₂ + d₃²V₃: 0.3² × 2 = 0.2² × 1.5 + 0.15² × V₃. So V₃ = (0.18 − 0.06) / 0.0225 ≈ 5.33 m/s.

questions.question: Water flows at 0.05 m³/s through a horizontal pipe that narrows from 200 mm to 100 mm diameter. Neglecting losses, the pressure drop between the two sections is approximately:

A horizontal venturimeter has an inlet diameter of 200 mm and a throat diameter of 100 mm. The difference in pressure head is 0.5 m of water and C_d = 0.98. Taking g = 9.81 m/s², the discharge is approximately:
Water issues from a small orifice under a head of 2.1 m. The jet travels 2 m horizontally while falling 0.5 m. The coefficient of velocity is approximately:
A pitot tube in a water stream shows a difference of 0.2 m between the stagnation head and the static head. Its coefficient is 0.98. Taking g = 9.81 m/s², the velocity of flow is approximately:

A tank of uniform cross-sectional area 4 m² is emptied through an orifice of area 0.01 m² at its bottom, with C_d = 0.6. The initial depth of water is 4 m. Taking g = 9.81 m/s², the time to empty the tank is approximately:
A two-dimensional flow has the stream function ψ = 2xy, with u = ∂ψ/∂y and v = −∂ψ/∂x. The magnitude of the velocity at the point (1, 2) is approximately:
An oil of kinematic viscosity 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ m²/s flows through a pipe of 25 mm diameter. Taking the critical Reynolds number as 2000, the greatest mean velocity for laminar flow is:
Water flows at 2 m/s through a pipe 500 m long and 200 mm in diameter. The Darcy friction factor (f in h_f = fLV²/2gd) is 0.02. Taking g = 9.81 m/s², the head lost in friction is approximately:
For laminar flow in a circular pipe at a Reynolds number of 1600, the Darcy friction factor (f = 64/Re) is:
An oil of viscosity 0.1 Pa·s flows in laminar flow at a mean velocity of 1 m/s through a horizontal pipe of 100 mm diameter. The pressure drop over a length of 100 m is:
questions.explanation: By the Hagen-Poiseuille equation, Δp = 32μVL / d² = 32 × 0.1 × 1 × 100 / 0.1² = 32000 Pa = 32 kPa.

questions.question: In a horizontal pipe of 80 mm diameter, the pressure drops by 20 kPa over a length of 50 m. The shear stress at the pipe wall is:
Water flowing at 4 m/s in a pipe meets a sudden enlargement, after which the velocity is 1 m/s. Taking g = 9.81 m/s², the head lost at the enlargement is approximately:

Two pipes in series are 500 m long and 0.3 m in diameter, and 300 m long and 0.2 m in diameter, with the same friction factor. By Dupuit's equation (L/D⁵ = Σ L/d⁵), the length of an equivalent pipe of 0.25 m diameter is approximately:
A pipeline delivers 0.1 m³/s of water from a reservoir with a gross head of 90 m. The friction loss is 30 m. Taking γ_w = 9.81 kN/m³, the power available at the outlet is:
questions.explanation: P = γQ(H − h_f) = 9.81 × 0.1 × (90 − 30) = 58.86 kW. (With h_f = H/3 this is the condition for maximum power.)

questions.question: Water flows at 2 m/s in a rigid pipe and a valve at the end is closed instantaneously. The velocity of the pressure wave is 1400 m/s. The rise in pressure due to water hammer is:
A spillway model is built to a scale of 1:25 and tested by Froude's law. If the prototype discharge is 1000 m³/s, the discharge in the model should be:
questions.explanation: For Froude similarity, Q_r = L_r^2.5. Q_m = 1000 / 25^2.5 = 1000 / 3125 = 0.32 m³/s.

questions.question: A rectangular channel 3 m wide carries water 1.5 m deep on a bed slope of 1 in 1000. Manning's n is 0.015. The discharge is approximately:
An open channel has a hydraulic radius of 0.8 m and a bed slope of 0.0005. With a Chezy constant of 50, the mean velocity is:
A rectangular channel of the most economical section has a flow area of 8 m². The depth of flow is:
questions.explanation: For the most economical rectangular section, b = 2y, so A = 2y² = 8 and y = 2.00 m (with b = 4 m).

questions.question: A trapezoidal channel of the most economical section has side slopes at 60° to the horizontal (half of a regular hexagon). If the flow area is 15.588 m², the depth of flow is approximately:
questions.explanation: For this section, A = √3 y². So y = √(15.588 / 1.732) = √9 = 3.00 m.

questions.question: A rectangular channel carries a discharge of 3 m³/s per metre width. Taking g = 9.81 m/s², the critical depth is approximately:
Water flows at 4 m/s in a rectangular channel at a depth of 0.5 m. Taking g = 9.81 m/s², the Froude number is approximately:
A hydraulic jump forms in a horizontal rectangular channel where the depth is 0.5 m and the velocity is 4 m/s. Taking g = 9.81 m/s², the depth after the jump is approximately:
In a hydraulic jump in a horizontal rectangular channel, the depths before and after the jump are 0.4 m and 2.0 m. The head lost in the jump is:
A 90° V-notch has a head of 0.2 m over its vertex and C_d = 0.6. Taking g = 9.81 m/s², the discharge is approximately:
A pump delivers 0.05 m³/s of water against a total head of 30 m with an overall efficiency of 75%. Taking γ_w = 9.81 kN/m³, the power input to the pump is:
questions.explanation: Water power = γQH = 9.81 × 0.05 × 30 = 14.72 kW. Input power = 14.72 / 0.75 = 19.62 kW.
